claim.pdf_says: Annex G / (informative) / Known errors / G.1  Rationale / G.2  List of errors  -- typeset identically to 'Annex F / (informative) / Archaic and obsolete language element lists / F.1 / F.2' on p.1229 (same centred bold annex title, same numbered-subclause style)
claim.markdown_says: specs/ISO_COBOL.md:49888 '# Annex G' (H1, with no anchor), then '## G.1 Rationale' / '## G.2 List of errors' -- versus lines 49823-49832 '' + '## Annex F' (H2) + '### F.1 Archaic language elements'
claim.why_it_matters: Annexes A-F are all '' + '## Annex X' (lines 38874, 40145, 41088, 41492, 48515, 49823). Annex G alone is promoted to H1 -- the level reserved for the per-page running header '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' -- and alone has no section anchor, so no '#section-annex-g' link target exists and any TOC/doc-map walker places Annex G at the wrong depth. Annex G is the standard's own known-errata list, which must be reachable like every other annex.

verdict.reasoning: Every mechanically checkable assertion in the claim was independently verified, and the one PDF-side assertion the claim rests on (typesetting parity with Annex F) was confirmed by rendering both pages. (1) PDF p.1231 rendered at 300dpi shows exactly: running header 'ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)', centred bold 'Annex G', centred '(informative)', centred bold 'Known errors', then left-aligned bold 'G.1  Rationale' and 'G.2  List of errors'. (2) PDF p.1229 rendered for comparison is typeset IDENTICALLY -- same centred bold annex label at the same size and vertical position, same '(informative)' line, same centred bold annex title, same left-aligned bold subclause heads. There is nothing in the PDF that distinguishes Annex G from Annex F or that would justify promoting it to a higher structural level; the promotion is purely a transcription artefact. (3) Markdown quotes are exact, not misquoted: 'grep -n "^#{1,3} Annex [A-H]$"' returns '## Annex A' (38875), '## Annex B' (40146), '## Annex C' (41089), '## Annex D' (41493), '## Annex E' (48516), '## Annex F' (49824), and '# Annex G' (49888) -- Annex G is the sole H1. 'grep -n id="section-annex-' returns anchors for a,b,c,d,e,f at 38874/40145/41088/41492/48515/49823 and NONE for g; no '#section-annex-g' target exists anywhere in the file. (4) The 'reserved level' point holds: of all H1 lines in the file, 941 are the running header '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' and 5 are cover/title-page lines; '# Annex G' is the only body heading at H1. So the anomaly is genuine, unique, and objectively verifiable -- this is not page-break furniture, line wrapping, or hyphenation. I nevertheless corrected the description on two points where the claim overstates or mislabels (see corrected_description): nothing is actually MISSING from the prose, and the G.1/G.2 subclause-level part of the claim is a pre-existing document-wide pattern rather than an Annex G anomaly.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL but mislabelled -- the correct kind is 'wrong-heading-level + missing-section-anchor', NOT 'missing-heading'. No heading text is missing: 'Annex G', '(informative)', 'Known errors', 'G.1 Rationale' and 'G.2 List of errors' are all present in the transcription in the correct order with correct text, and a full sentence-by-sentence comparison of the p.1231 render against page-1231.md shows the entire page body (the G.1 lead paragraph, all three em-dash bullets, the G.2 lead-in, item 1) Accessibility with sub-items a) through g), and item 2) Mapping of uppercase letters to lowercase letters including 'Changes_When_Lowercased' and 'UAX #44, Unicode 13.0.0') is transcribed completely and accurately. The genuine defect is confined to markup structure, and has exactly two parts: (a) line 49888 is '# Annex G' at H1 where Annexes A-F are all '## Annex X' at H2 -- H1 is otherwise used only for the 941 per-page running headers and 5 cover-page lines, so Annex G is the sole body heading colliding with the running-header level; and (b) Annex G alone lacks the '' anchor that precedes every other annex title, so no '#section-annex-g' link target exists. Repair: replace line 49888 '# Annex G' with '' on its own line followed by '## Annex G'. DROP the G.1/G.2 subclause-level element of the claim: '## G.1' / '## G.2' being H2 rather than H3 is NOT unique to Annex G -- '## A.2' (39466), '## A.3' (39672), '## D.3' (42371) and '## E.3' (48904) are H2 as well, so subclause-depth drift is a pre-existing document-wide inconsistency and citing it here is misleading. Severity is correctly 'structural' but strictly navigational: no normative or informative spec text is lost or altered, and Annex G is an informative annex, so no COBOL semantics are affected -- the impact is limited to TOC/doc-map walkers placing Annex G at the wrong depth and cross-references to '#section-annex-g' having no target.
